q: Say "plate." Change /p/ to /s/. What word do you hear?
e: Plate with /s/ in place of /p/ is slate.

q: Say "stamp." Take away /t/. What word is left?
Say "block." Change /l/ to /r/. What word do you say?
e: Replacing l with r gives brock.

q: Which word has a variant vowel sound like "oo" in "moon"?
Which word has a trigraph at the beginning?
e: Three begins with the three-letter blend thr.

q: Which word has a silent letter?
e: The k is silent in knife.

q: Which word has a silent "g"?
e: The g is silent in gnat.

q: Which word has a closed syllable?
e: The first syllable in pocket is closed.

q: Which word has a VCe syllable?
The contraction for "do not" is...
e: Don't uses an apostrophe for the missing o.

q: How can you split the word "rabbit" into syllables?
e: Rabbit splits between the two b's.

q: What does the prefix un- mean in "unlock"?
What does the prefix re- mean in "redo"?
Which is a word readers see often?
Which contraction is spelled correctly?
e: Can't has the apostrophe after n.

q: Which tool tells you how to say a word and what it means?
e: A dictionary gives pronunciation and meaning.

q: A glossary in a book is found...
o: at the back and lists important words

q: "The huge elephant stomped. It was gigantic." What does gigantic mean?
"Mia was famished after the long hike, so she ate three sandwiches." What does famished mean?
e: The sandwiches show she was hungry.

q: What does the suffix -ful mean in "careful"?
What does the suffix -less mean in "hopeless"?
What does the prefix dis- mean in "disagree"?
Which word is a synonym for "big"?
e: Large means the same as big.

q: Which word is an antonym of "hot"?
e: Cold is the opposite of hot.

q: Which pair are homophones?
"I need to check the bark of the tree." Bark here means...
o: the rough outside of a tree

q: Why might you read a book of animal facts before a zoo trip?
You are about to read about volcanoes. Which question helps?
The title is "The Snowy Day." The cover shows a boy in boots. What do you predict?
o: the boy plays in the snow
the boy bakes in the sun
the boy swims in a pool
e: The cover and title give clues.

q: "The sky was a deep purple as the sun melted into the hills." What do you picture?
A story about moving to a new school reminds you of your first day. This is...
e: You linked it to your life.

q: Sam grabs a towel and runs to the lake. What can you infer?
e: The towel and lake suggest swimming.

q: Read: "Seeds need water, light, and soil to grow." What is the key idea?
One page says frogs lay eggs in water. Another says tadpoles breathe with gills. What can you conclude?
e: Combining facts shows water is first.

q: You read a paragraph and are confused. What should you try?
o: reread it and think about what it says

q: A story about a lost puppy makes you think of your pet. What is this?
e: You linked it to your life.

q: Which is a good brief comment about a book?
o: I liked how the story showed friendship.

q: Why did the child cry? "Jo cried because her kite broke." Where is the evidence?
o: in the sentence about the kite

q: Which is the best paraphrase of "The bright sun warmed the whole village"?
o: The sun made the village warm.

q: When you retell a story, you should include...
e: A retell has the key parts.

q: A boy keeps trying to ride a bike and finally succeeds. What is the theme?
Lila is nervous but still speaks to the class. What does this show?
In a story, the problem is solved at the end. This part is the...
Why is the setting "a dark cave" important to a scary story?
A story where animals talk and a lesson is taught is a...
A story that starts "Once upon a time" and has magic is a...
A poem is shaped like a tree on the page. What does this do?
In a play, the words the characters say are called...
A text says, "Owls hunt at night. They have great eyesight. They hear small sounds." What is the central idea?
e: All sentences are about owls hunting.

q: Where would you look to find where a section on "Habitats" begins?
e: The table of contents lists sections.

q: A text explains that because it rained, the grass grew. The text structure is...
An ad says, "Buy our juice! It is the best!" What does it want you to do?
e: The ad tries to persuade you.

q: Which sentence is a fact?
o: A giraffe is the tallest land animal.

q: Which sentence is an opinion?
o: Pizza is baked in an oven.

q: Why did the author write a book called "How to Plant a Garden"?
A book lists steps in order. This structure helps the author...
What does a diagram with labels help the reader do?
"The wind whispered through the trees." This uses...
Which phrase is figurative?
e: It compares a person to a bee.

q: "I felt happy when I won." Which point of view is this?
"She felt happy when she won." Which point of view is this?
The poem says "Run, run, run, as fast as you can." What is repeated?
Which sentence is a good topic sentence for a paragraph about dogs?
e: A topic sentence tells the main idea.

q: Which detail best supports "Dogs make great pets"?
e: Details back up the main idea.

q: Which revision adds a good detail to "The boy ran."?
o: The tall boy ran across the muddy field.

q: Which sentence has the verb that agrees?
Which sentence uses the future tense?
Which word completes the sentence in the past? "Yesterday, I ___ to the store."
Which word is a common noun?
Which shows the plural of "child"?
Which sentence uses an adjective?
Which word is an adverb that tells where?
Which word is an adverb that tells when?
Which phrase is a prepositional phrase?
e: A prepositional phrase begins with a preposition.

q: Choose the right pronoun: "___ is my friend."
Which is a possessive pronoun?
Which sentence uses a coordinating conjunction to join two subjects?
Which word is a coordinating conjunction?
Which of these needs a capital letter?
e: Months and days of the week are capitalized.

q: Which punctuation mark ends the greeting in a friendly letter?
e: A greeting ends with a comma.

q: Which is written correctly?
Which sentence uses commas in a list correctly?
o: I like, apples grapes and pears.
I like apples, grapes, and pears.
I like apples, grapes and, pears.
I like apples grapes, and pears.
e: Commas separate items in a list.

q: Which is a good start for a personal narrative?
o: Last winter, I learned to skate.
e: A personal narrative tells about your own life.

q: A how-to paragraph about brushing teeth should include...
A thank-you note should include...
o: a greeting, a thank you, and a closing
e: These are the parts of a note.
